repair_delta.rationale: The referenced blind-run artifact is a prior observed occurrence. Current V0.3 recurrence vocabulary has no OBSERVED_TEST; OBSERVED_HISTORY is the narrowest canonical recurrence class.

support_summary: Agent evaluations should combine grader types appropriate to the task rather than rely on one proxy.
Model-based graders capture nuance but require calibration with human graders.
For research agents, groundedness, coverage and source-quality checks can be combined with LLM rubrics; LLM rubrics should be calibrated against expert judgment.
Capability/quality evals and regression evals serve different purposes.
Independent third-party evaluation provides additional evidence for capability/safeguard claims.
Evaluation reports should state the claim tested and evidence of validity.
Known validity hazards include reward hacking, contamination, broken problems and sandbagging.
Harness and budget can materially change measured capability, so evaluation claims must be bound to the tested setup.
Visible/automated grading can create strong pressure to satisfy the grader rather than the underlying intent.
The reported experiments show reward-hacking behavior generalizing to grader/reward tampering.
This supports avoiding a producer-visible simplistic novelty/WOW proxy as the acceptance target.
